newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK residential prices seen down in Q3 - Lehman.
newsitem.headline: HK residential prices seen down in Q3 - Lehman.

text.p: Hong Kong residential prices are likely to fall three to five percent in the third quarter and stay flat during the fourth quarter, following expected government measures to cool down rising prices, Lehman Brothers said on Tuesday.
Analyst Michael Leary told a Lehman Brothers seminar that the drops would bring full-year growth for the market to 10 percent in 1997.
However, strong demand should generate growth again in 1998, when prices were expected to grow 10 percent, and the supply and demand situation should lead to a rise of five percent in 1999, he said.
Britain hands the British colony back to China at midnight on June 30. The post-handover government is expected to launch measures to curb residential property prices.
Analyst Raymond Lee said the territory's banks faced no immediate danger although they had been increasing their focus on residential mortage lending over the last decade.
"I don't think there is immediate concern to an alarming scale," he added.
However, Hong Kong banks were expected to restructure their mix of loans, he said, with the focus shifting away from property lending.
"I think structurally banks in Hong Kong are very likely to go through a fairly dramatic change in the mix of loans," said Lee. "Manufacturing is a clear area that banks will go for."
Home mortgages take up 25 percent of Hong Kong banks' loan portfolio, to which manufacturing contribute only six percent at present, Lee said.
